title: Indian Army Chief Concludes Nepal Visit, Discussions Focused on Defense Cooperation - Ratopati
description: Indian Army Chief Concludes Nepal Visit, Discussions Focused on Defense Cooperation  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth has returned to his country after concluding his four-day visit to Nepal.

Invited by Nepali Army Chief Ashok Sigdel, he arrived in Nepal on July 17 and met with President Ramchandra Paudel, Prime Minister Balen Shah, and Chief of Army Staff Sigdel. During his visit, he visited Pashupatinath and traveled to Pokhara.

The four-day visit schedule of the Indian Army Chief was generally limited to formalities. However, experts say this visit has opened the door for high-level visits between the two countries.

The meeting between Prime Minister Balen Shah and Indian Army Chief Seth is considered significant. Prime Minister Balen does not usually grant audiences to foreign representatives. Even when Seth was honored with the title of 'Honorary General' at the Presidential Palace on August 17, Prime Minister Balen, who also holds the portfolio of Defense Minister, was not present. Prime Ministers have attended every such honorary conferment ceremony in the past.

However, the following day (August 18), Prime Minister Balen met with Indian Army Chief Seth. The Indian Ambassador to Nepal, Naveen Srivastava, was also present at the meeting. Some interpret this meeting as Prime Minister Balen breaking his stance and continuity. Others have expressed the view that military diplomacy between Nepal and India has been successful.

Chief of Army Staff Sigdel met with Prime Minister Balen twice before the visit of Indian Army Chief Seth. It is rumored that he was the one who facilitated the meeting between the Indian Army Chief Seth and Prime Minister Balen.

This was the highest-level visit from India since the formation of the government under Prime Minister Balen's leadership. Seth's first foreign visit after being appointed Army Chief was to Nepal. This also confirms the importance given to the visit by both countries.

Dr. Indra Adhikari, an expert in defense and diplomatic affairs, stated that military diplomacy has opened a closed door between Nepal and India. She believes this has paved the way for other high-level visits. She explained that the meeting between India's Army Chief Seth and Prime Minister Balen, at a time when Prime Minister Balen has been reluctant to meet foreign representatives due to protocol, is a significant example of successful military diplomacy in Nepal.

She further stated that military diplomacy has helped mend relations between Nepal and India at a time when relations have been strained repeatedly, and the recent events are a part of that process.

Adhikari mentioned that the emotional bond between the two countries is strengthened by the fact that the army chiefs of both countries are honorary generals of each other's nations. She added that this is why the Nepali Army has stepped forward in every difficult situation between the two countries.

What was discussed in the meeting?

During the meeting between Prime Minister Balen and Army Chief Seth, discussions were held on strengthening the relationship between the two countries. A press release issued by the Indian Embassy in Nepal stated, 'General Seth paid a courtesy call on the Honourable Prime Minister of Nepal, where the discussion focused on the long-standing partnership between the two countries, especially in defense cooperation.'

It was reported that discussions were held on continuing military cooperation and ongoing military exercises between the two countries.

Nepali Army spokesperson Rajaram Basnet said that Army Chief Seth, who came to Nepal for the traditional honorary general conferment, discussed military cooperation, military exercises, and assistance between the two countries. He added that he had no information about any other discussions.

The recruitment of Gurkha soldiers between Nepal and India has been suspended for a long time. Following India's Agnipath scheme, the recruitment of Nepali citizens into the Indian Army has been halted. Despite repeated requests from India for recruitment, Nepal has not been ready for it. However, there was no discussion on this matter during the visit.

Spokesperson Basnet also stated that there was no discussion on this matter with the Nepali Army. Sources from the Prime Minister's Office also indicated that there was no discussion regarding the recruitment of Gurkha soldiers (Agniveer).

Sources from the Prime Minister's Office claim that apart from continuing military cooperation and advancing collaboration in various fields, there were no other discussions.

Nepali Army's Diplomatic Practice

The Nepali Army has resolved strained relations between Nepal and India through military diplomacy not only now but also in the past. In recent times, the distance between Nepal and India has been increasing due to border disputes, visits, and diplomatic meetings. A retired Lieutenant General of the Nepali Army stated that India's effort to bring the Army Chief Seth to Nepal was an attempt to reduce that distance.

Whenever a crisis arises between Nepal and India, the Nepali Army has stepped forward. During the Indian blockade imposed on Nepal in 2015, the blockade was lifted after the then Chief of Army Staff of Nepal, Rajendra Chhetri, visited India.

After that, the then Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli visited India. He received a grand welcome in India. According to a retired Lieutenant General, the Nepali Army had undertaken a mission to lift the blockade. The Nepali Army had sent a team to India at that time to study the Madhesh movement in the Terai region and discuss it with the Indian side.

The source said, 'A team led by then Lieutenant General Himal Thapa, considered a confidant of then Chief of Army Staff Chhetri, reached Delhi, India. They stayed in India for two weeks, holding discussions and meetings with various individuals. Only after receiving assurances of lifting the blockade did then Chief of Army Staff Chhetri travel to Delhi and successfully lift the blockade.'

In a conversation with the National News Agency (November 2024), retired Lieutenant General Himal Thapa had said, 'The Indian Army has also assisted Nepal in lifting past blockades. It can be taken as an example that if any political issues arise, they can be addressed through military diplomacy. The relationship between Nepal and India is multifaceted. The relationship established at the military level between Nepal and India is becoming a strong example for the world in the field of military diplomacy.'

Oli's Effort

During the blockade, then Prime Minister Oli had repeatedly sent then Foreign Minister Kamal Thapa to India. To lift the blockade, Foreign Minister Kamal Thapa visited India three times: twice in October 2015 and once in November 2015. Thapa met with Indian spiritual leader Sri Ravi Shankar, then Foreign Minister Sushma Swaraj, and other leaders.

However, when it was not possible to lift the blockade, Prime Minister Oli sought the help of the Nepali Army. Oli disregarded then Foreign Minister Thapa and improved relations with India with the help of the army, which led to a deterioration in relations between Oli and Thapa at that time.

Thapa was not present at the press conference held by Oli before his visit to India. There was speculation that Thapa might not be included in Oli's delegation, but in the end, he also accompanied Oli to India.

The Nepali Army has not only lifted the blockade but has also resolved misunderstandings between India and Nepal in recent times. According to military sources, India did not favor then Prime Minister Oli due to border disputes. Prime Minister Oli made repeated attempts to visit India.

For this, he also sent his envoys to India. Then Foreign Minister Dr. Arzu Rana Deuba also made efforts, but it was not possible through anyone. At that time too, India softened its stance due to the initiative of the Nepali Army, and Oli's visit to India was scheduled. While preparations for the visit were underway, the Genji movement occurred, and the government led by Oli collapsed.

According to military diplomats, Prachanda, the coordinator of the Nepali Communist Party, also sought the help of the Nepali Army to improve relations with India. Prachanda, who resigned as Prime Minister in the case of then Chief of Army Staff Rukmangad Katuwal, had realized the importance of the Nepali Army at that time. After becoming Prime Minister, he improved relations with India with the help of the Nepali Army, according to knowledgeable sources.

Basanta Khadka wrote in Unity Journal, 'While the government is doing important work in expanding diplomatic relations with neighboring and friendly countries, the Nepali Army is also advancing military diplomacy in its own way with the military personnel of neighboring and friendly countries. Military partnerships, training, equipment, and knowledge exchange with America, Britain, China, and India in recent times are examples of this.'

The Pacific Command training with America, the Sagarmatha joint military training with China, and the Surya Kiran training with India are some of the recent efforts by the army through military diplomacy to expand the country's relations and partnerships. This is also considered a success for the Nepali Army in military diplomacy.

title: An ever-booming Nepali diaspora is being served by severely understaffed missions - The Kathmandu Post
description: An ever-booming Nepali diaspora is being served by severely understaffed missions  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepal’s diplomatic missions abroad are struggling with staff shortages as the number of Nepalis living, working and studying overseas continues to rise. This has increased pressure on consular services and limited the missions’ ability to pursue broader diplomatic and economic goals.

The government has repeatedly pledged to strengthen its missions to promote exports, bilateral trade and investment, tourism and economic diplomacy. But missions in countries with rapidly growing Nepali communities say they lack the personnel and resources to deliver even routine services efficiently, let alone pursue those wider objectives.

Japan offers one of the starkest examples.

Nepal opened its embassy in Tokyo in 1965, when roughly 1,000 Nepalis lived in Japan. The mission began with three diplomatic staff. Six decades later, the Nepali community has grown to about 342,000, but the diplomatic establishment has barely changed.

The embassy has five diplomatic positions, including the ambassador. With the ambassadorial post vacant for the past 11 months, only four diplomatic staff are currently working there. Just one position was added last year.

“There were three staff members 61 years ago. Now there are four of us,” Harihar Kant Poudel, chargé d’affaires ad interim, said. “The Nepali diaspora is growing every day, but the resources and staffing of the embassy have not increased accordingly.”

The increase has been particularly rapid in recent years. Japan had about 97,000 Nepalis in 2021, according to the embassy. By August 2026, the number has risen to around 342,000.

The growing population has brought a sharp increase in demand for passports, document verification, powers of attorney and other consular services. The embassy issued about 19,000 passports in the last fiscal year.

Three years ago, applicants would generally receive services on the same day. The embassy now often asks them to leave their documents and return later.

“The workload is so heavy that we are busy even on weekly holidays,” Paudel said.

The pressure is also affecting the embassy’s ability to respond to emergencies. Seventy-three Nepali citizens died in Japan last year for various reasons. The embassy had to assist with the administrative and legal procedures following their deaths, including compensation claims and arrangements concerning their remains, including repatriation. Staff sometimes struggle to visit hospitals and police stations because they are tied up with routine consular work.

The embassy has repeatedly asked the foreign ministry for two additional diplomatic staff and two local employees. It has also sought more resources to assess and verify worker demand, inspect employers, address labour disputes, protect workers’ rights and visit immigration detention centres and prisons to check on Nepali detainees.

Economic diplomacy has suffered. Japan is a major development partner and an important potential source of investment and trade, but embassy officials say they have little time to pursue those opportunities.

Last year, funds allocated by the foreign ministry for economic diplomacy went unused because the mission’s limited staff were occupied with routine consular services.

The embassy in Australia faces similar problems.

Nepal opened its embassy in Canberra in 2007, when only about 7,000 to 8,000 Nepalis lived in Australia. The community now numbers around 300,000. The mission also serves Nepalis in Fiji, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea and other countries in the region.

The mission has four diplomatic staff apart from the ambassador, although the ambassadorial position has also been vacant for months.

Tara Gautam, chargé d’affaires ad interim, said hundreds of people visit the embassy for passports, consular services and powers of attorney.

About 150 people come to the embassy each day for passports alone, and staff must process their photographs and biometric data. More than ten applications for powers of attorney, which must be certified by the head of mission, are also received daily.

“I thought the workload would be lighter here than in Saudi Arabia, where I previously worked,” Gautam said. “But it is not. The resources and staff are insufficient for the number of people we serve.”

The embassy has repeatedly requested additional staff.

Foreign Ministry officials acknowledge that most Nepali missions have been operating with bare minimum staff for years.

Lok Bahadur Poudel Chhetri, spokesperson for the foreign ministry, said the missions were expected to promote Nepal’s interests abroad, economic diplomacy, trade and Nepali culture, while also taking on growing responsibilities for the welfare and protection of Nepalis overseas.

“Our missions are providing maximum services with minimum staff,” he said.

Nepal currently has missions at 45 locations, including embassies in 31 countries, three permanent missions to the UN and other organisations, and ten consulates general, along with a field office in Visakhapatnam, India.

In its budget speech in May, the government announced plans to close the embassies in Denmark, Brazil and South Africa, the consulates general in Chengdu and San Francisco, and the field office in Visakhapatnam. The closures have yet to be completed.

Experts say Nepal’s missions abroad, operating with barely enough staff to function, cannot be expected to deliver on the government’s economic diplomacy ambitions.

Former foreign secretary Madan Kumar Bhattarai says strengthening missions in countries where the Nepali population and economic ties have grown rapidly is essential.

“Where there is greater need and a heavier workload, staffing and other resources should be increased,” he said. “Given the country’s limited financial capacity, priorities should be based on the size of the Nepali diaspora and the economic, commercial, social and cultural importance of each country.”

Staffing levels vary considerably among missions.

The Nepali mission in the United Arab Emirates serves a community of around 700,000 Nepalis. The consulate general in Dubai has only four staff, including the consul general.

Several smaller missions, including those in Myanmar, Brazil, Spain, Denmark and South Africa, have only an ambassador and two diplomatic staff positions. Missions in Ottawa (Canada), Islamabad (Pakistan), Cairo (Egypt), Colombo (Sri Lanka), Tel Aviv (Israel), Paris (France), Berlin (Germany), Brussels (Belgium), Muscat (Oman), Manama (Bahrain), Moscow (Russia), Lisbon (Portugal) and Vienna (Austria) generally have an ambassador and three diplomatic staff. The consulate general in Jeddah (Saudi Arabia) has four staff apart from the consul general.

The embassies in Canberra, Tokyo, Dhaka (Bangladesh), Bangkok (Thailand) and Seoul (South Korea) each have four diplomatic staff positions apart from the ambassador.

Nepal opened its first overseas mission in London in 1934. It currently has five diplomatic staff apart from the ambassador. Nepal’s embassy in Abu Dhabi (UAE) has eight staff, Kuwait seven, Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia) nine, Doha (Qatar) nine, Riyadh (Saudi Arabia) eight and Washington, DC, seven.

Nepal’s permanent mission to the UN in New York has 11 staff, while its permanent missions in Geneva and Vienna have seven and three, respectively. The Nepali consulate general in Kolkata has six staff.

Across all 45 missions, there are currently 244 approved positions, including ambassadors and consul generals. Of these, 47 are held by officials from outside the Foreign Service. They include seven joint secretaries from the civil administration service, seven military attachés, one police counsellor, one intelligence counsellor, nine administrative undersecretaries, two revenue undersecretaries, one legal undersecretary, one accounts undersecretary, nine administrative section officers, three accounts officers, one revenue section officer and five administrative/accounts assistants.

In addition to Foreign Service personnel sent by the ministry, the missions also hire local staff. These include office secretaries, legal advisers, messengers, translators, gardeners, security guards and office assistants, among others.

There are 374 approved positions for local employees. The Foreign Employment Board had been providing financial support for local staff at missions in countries with large numbers of Nepali migrant workers, including Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Malaysia. The board had been spending Rs25.7 million annually to fund 19 local employees at various embassies. But after the Office of the Auditor General deemed the arrangement contrary to rules, the number of board-funded staff was cut from last year, further increasing the workload on the limited diplomatic staff.

The government has conducted new organisational and management (O&M) surveys for all 17 ministries. Because the surveys were aimed at cutting public expenditure, the Foreign Ministry has been unable to add positions despite its requests for more staff.

The ministry has sought to transfer foreign service staff from the six missions proposed for closure to embassies where additional personnel are needed. However, because the O&M restructuring has not yet been certified by the Prime Minister’s Office, the ministry’s plan has yet to materialise. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Chhetri said the ministry wants to transfer staff from missions proposed for closure to those in need without imposing additional financial burden on the state.

Under the proposal, the ministry would also cut positions in the administration, revenue and accounts groups at missions and replace them with Foreign Service personnel. It has proposed scrapping two minister (economic) positions at the Nepali embassies in New Delhi and Beijing, five consul-general positions in Hong Kong, Lhasa, Kolkata, Chengdu and Guangzhou, and seven joint-secretary-level positions from the administrative service.

It has also proposed cutting labour counsellor positions in the general administration group in Seoul, Kuala Lumpur, Riyadh, Doha and Abu Dhabi, along with the cultural counsellor in New Delhi, the economic counsellor in Visakhapatnam, and nine administrative undersecretary positions, including those from the revenue group in Washington, DC, and Kolkata. The proposal also calls for cutting ten administrative section officer positions at various missions.

Officials from the administrative service have opposed the proposed cuts. Pressure from the administrative service has also meant that Chief Secretary Govinda Bahadur Karki has yet to certify the Foreign Ministry’s O&M proposal.

सरकार बेर-बेर निर्यात, द्विपक्षीय व्यापार आ निवेश, पर्यटन आ आर्थिक कूटनीति कए बढ़ावा देबा लेल अपन मिशन कए मजबूत करबाक वचन देलक अछि। लेकिन तेजी स॑ बढ़त॑ जाय रहलऽ नेपाली समुदाय वाला देशऽ के मिशनऽ के कहना छै कि ओकरा पास वू व्यापक उद्देश्य क॑ पूरा करना त॑ दूर, नियमित सेवा भी कुशलता स॑ दै लेली कर्मी आरू संसाधन के कमी छै ।

जापान एकर एकटा शुद्ध उदाहरण दैत अछि।

नेपाल १९६५ मे टोक्यो मे अपन दूतावास खोललक, जखन जापान मे लगभग १,००० नेपाली रहैत छल । मिशन के शुरुआत तीन कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी स भेल। छह दशक बाद नेपाली समुदाय लगभग ३ लाख ४२ हजार भ गेल अछि, मुदा कूटनीतिक प्रतिष्ठान मे मुश्किल स परिवर्तन भेल अछि ।

दूतावास के पांच कूटनीतिक पद अछि, जाहि मे राजदूत सेहो शामिल अछि. पिछला 11 महीना स राजदूत पद खाली रहला स एखन ओतय मात्र चारिटा कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी काज क रहल छथि। पिछला साल बस एकटा पद जोड़ल गेल छल।

चार्ज डी’अफेयर्स एड इंटरिम हरिहर कांत पौडेल कहलनि जे, 61 साल पहिने तीनटा कर्मचारी छल, आब हम चारि गोटे छी। “नेपाली प्रवासी सब दिन बढ़ि रहल अछि, मुदा दूतावासक संसाधन आ कर्मचारी मे तदनुसार वृद्धि नहि भेल अछि।”

हाल के साल मे ई बढ़ोतरी खास क तेजी सं भेल अछि. दूतावास के अनुसार जापान मे २०२१ मे करीब ९७ हजार नेपाली छल । अगस्त 2026 तक ई संख्या बढ़ि कए करीब 342,000 भ गेल अछि।

बढ़तऽ आबादी के कारण पासपोर्ट, दस्तावेज सत्यापन, पावर ऑफ अटॉर्नी आरू अन्य कांसुलर सेवा के मांग म॑ भारी वृद्धि होय गेलऽ छै । दूतावास पिछला वित्तीय वर्ष मे करीब 19 हजार पासपोर्ट जारी केलक अछि।

तीन साल पहिने आवेदक कए आम तौर पर एकहि दिन सेवा भेटैत छल। दूतावास आब अक्सरहां हुनका सभ सं कहैत अछि जे ओ अपन कागजात छोड़ि कs बाद मे वापस आबि जाउ.

पौडेल कहलनि जे, काजक बोझ एतेक भारी अछि जे साप्ताहिक छुट्टी मे सेहो हम सब व्यस्त रहैत छी।

दबाव के असर दूतावास के आपातकालीन स्थिति के जवाब देबय के क्षमता पर सेहो पड़ि रहल अछि. जापानमे विगत वर्ष विभिन्न कारणसँ ३३ नेपाली नागरिकके मृत्यु भेल छल । दूतावास क॑ हुनकऽ मौत के बाद प्रशासनिक आरू कानूनी प्रक्रिया म॑ सहायता करना छेलै, जेकरा म॑ मुआवजा के दावा आरू हुनकऽ अवशेष स॑ संबंधित व्यवस्था शामिल छेलै, जेकरा म॑ वापसी भी शामिल छेलै । कर्मचारी कए कखनो काल अस्पताल आ थाना मे जेबा मे परेशानी होइत छनि, किया कि ओ नियमित कांसुलर काज स बान्हल रहैत छथि।

दूतावास बेर-बेर विदेश मंत्रालय स दूटा अतिरिक्त कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी आ दूटा स्थानीय कर्मचारी मांगने अछि। मजदूर के मांग के आकलन आ सत्यापन, नियोक्ता के निरीक्षण, श्रम विवाद के निपटारा, मजदूर के अधिकार के रक्षा आ आप्रवासन हिरासत केंद्र आ जेल में जा क नेपाली हिरासत में लेल गेल लोक के हालचाल के जांच सेहो केलक अछि।

आर्थिक कूटनीति के नुकसान भेल अछि। जापान विकास केरऽ एगो प्रमुख भागीदार आरू निवेश आरू व्यापार केरऽ एगो महत्वपूर्ण संभावित स्रोत छै, लेकिन दूतावास केरऽ अधिकारियऽ के कहना छै कि ओकरा पास वू अवसरऽ के पीछा करै लेली कम समय छै ।

पिछला साल विदेश मंत्रालय द्वारा आर्थिक कूटनीति के लेल आवंटित धन के उपयोग नहिं भ गेल छल, किया कि मिशन के सीमित कर्मचारी नियमित कांसुलर सेवा में व्यस्त छल.

ऑस्ट्रेलिया मे दूतावास कए सेहो एहने समस्या क सामना करय पड़ैत अछि।

नेपाल २००७ मे कैनबरा मे अपन दूतावास खोललक, जखन ऑस्ट्रेलिया मे मात्र लगभग ७,००० सँ ८,००० नेपाली रहैत छल । आब एहि समुदाय क संख्या करीब तीन लाख अछि। ई मिशन फिजी, न्यूजीलैंड, पापुआ न्यू गिनी आरू क्षेत्र केरऽ अन्य देशऽ के नेपाली सिनी के सेवा भी दै ​​छै ।

मिशन म॑ राजदूत के अलावा चार कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी छै, हालांकि राजदूत केरऽ पद भी महीना भर स॑ खाली छै ।

चार्ज डी’अफेयर्स एड इंटरिम तारा गौतम न॑ कहलकै कि पासपोर्ट, कांसुलर सेवा आरू पावर ऑफ अटॉर्नी लेली सैकड़ों लोग दूतावास म॑ जाय छै ।

असगर पासपोर्ट के लेल हर दिन करीब 150 लोक दूतावास मे अबैत छथि, आओर कर्मचारी के अपन फोटो आओर बायोमेट्रिक डाटा के प्रोसेस करय पड़त. पावर ऑफ अटॉर्नी के लेल दस सं बेसि आवेदन सेहो रोजाना मिलैत अछि, जेकरा मिशन के प्रमुख के प्रमाणित करय पड़त.

गौतम कहला जे हमरा लागल जे एहि ठाम काजक बोझ सऊदी अरब स हल्का होएत, जतय हम पहिने काज केने रही। “मुदा से नहि अछि। हम जतेक लोकक सेवा करैत छी ताहि लेल संसाधन आ कर्मचारी अपर्याप्त अछि।”

दूतावास बेर-बेर अतिरिक्त कर्मचारीक आग्रह केलक अछि।

विदेश मंत्रालय के अधिकारी सब स्वीकार करैत छथि जे अधिकांश नेपाली मिशन सालों स न्यूनतम कर्मचारी के संग संचालित भ रहल अछि।

विदेश मंत्रालय के प्रवक्ता लोकबहादुर पौडेल क्षेत्री कहलनि जे, एहि मिशन सं विदेश मे नेपाल के हित, आर्थिक कूटनीति, व्यापार आ नेपाली संस्कृति के बढ़ावा देबय के उम्मीद अछि, संगहि विदेश मे नेपाली के कल्याण आ सुरक्षा के बढ़ैत जिम्मेदारी सेहो उठाबय के उम्मीद अछि.

ओ कहला जे हमर मिशन न्यूनतम कर्मचारी क संग अधिकतम सेवा उपलब्ध करा रहल अछि।

नेपाल केरऽ अभी ४५ स्थानऽ प॑ मिशन छै, जेकरा म॑ ३१ देशऽ के दूतावास, संयुक्त राष्ट्र आरू अन्य संगठनऽ म॑ तीन स्थायी मिशन, आरू दस महावाणिज्य दूतावास के साथ-साथ भारत केरऽ विशाखापत्तनम म॑ फील्ड कार्यालय भी छै ।

मई म॑ अपनऽ बजट भाषण म॑ सरकार न॑ डेनमार्क, ब्राजील आरू दक्षिण अफ्रीका केरऽ दूतावास, चेंगदू आरू सैन फ्रांसिस्को केरऽ महावाणिज्य दूतावास आरू विशाखापत्तनम म॑ फील्ड ऑफिस बंद करै के योजना के घोषणा करलकै । एखन धरि बंदी पूरा नहि भ सकल अछि।

विशेषज्ञ के कहनाय छनि जे नेपाल के विदेश मे मिशन, जे मुश्किल सं एतेक कर्मचारी के संग संचालित भ रहल अछि जे सरकार के आर्थिक कूटनीति महत्वाकांक्षा के पूरा करय के उम्मीद नहिं कएल जा सकैत अछि.

पूर्व विदेश सचिव मदन कुमार भट्टराई नेपाली जनसंख्या आ आर्थिक सम्बन्ध मे तेजी सँ वृद्धि भेल देश मे मिशन सुदृढ करब आवश्यक बतौलनि ।

ओ कहला जे जतय बेसी जरूरत अछि आ काजक बोझ बेसी अछि, ओतय कर्मचारी आ अन्य संसाधन बढ़ेबाक चाही। “देश के सीमित वित्तीय क्षमता के देखैत प्राथमिकता नेपाली प्रवासी के आकार आ प्रत्येक देश के आर्थिक, वाणिज्यिक, सामाजिक आ सांस्कृतिक महत्व के आधार पर होबाक चाही।”

मिशनक कें बीच स्टाफिंग कें स्तर काफी भिन्न छै.

संयुक्त अरब अमीरात मे नेपाली मिशन लगभग ७ लाख नेपाली के समुदाय के सेवा दैत अछि । दुबई मे महावाणिज्य दूतावास मे मात्र चारिटा कर्मचारी छथि, जाहि मे महावाणिज्य दूत सेहो शामिल छथि।

म्यांमार, ब्राजील, स्पेन, डेनमार्क आरू दक्षिण अफ्रीका सहित कई छोटऽ मिशनऽ म॑ खाली एगो राजदूत आरू दू कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी केरऽ पद छै । ओटावा (कनाडा), इस्लामाबाद (पाकिस्तान), काहिरा (मिस्र), कोलंबो (श्रीलंका), तेल अवीव (इजरायल), पेरिस (फ्रांस), बर्लिन (जर्मनी), ब्रसेल्स (बेल्जियम), मस्कट (ओमान), मनामा (बहरीन), मास्को (रूस), लिस्बन (पुर्तगाल) आरू वियना (ऑस्ट्रिया) म॑ आम तौर प॑ एगो राजदूत आरू... तीन कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी। जेद्दाह (सऊदी अरब) केरऽ महावाणिज्य दूतावास म॑ महावाणिज्य दूत के अलावा चार कर्मचारी छै ।

कैनबरा, टोक्यो, ढाका (बांग्लादेश), बैंकॉक (थाईलैंड) आरू सियोल (दक्षिण कोरिया) केरऽ दूतावासऽ म॑ राजदूत के अलावा चार-चारि कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी केरऽ पद छै ।

नेपाल 1934 मे लंदन मे अपन पहिल विदेश मिशन खोललक।अखन राजदूत के अलावा पांच कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी अछि। अबू धाबी (यूएई) मे नेपालक दूतावास मे आठ कर्मचारी, कुवैत मे सात, कुआलालंपुर (मलेशिया) मे नौ, दोहा (कतार) मे नौ, रियाद (सऊदी अरब) मे आठ आ वाशिंगटन डी.सी.

न्यूयॉर्क म॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र म॑ नेपाल केरऽ स्थायी मिशन म॑ ११ कर्मचारी छै, जबकि जेनेवा आरू वियना म॑ ओकरऽ स्थायी मिशन म॑ क्रमशः सात आरू तीन कर्मचारी छै । कोलकातामे रहल नेपाली महावाणिज्य दूतावासमे ६ कर्मचारी अछि ।

सब 45 मिशनऽ म॑ अभी २४४ मंजूर पद छै, जेकरा म॑ राजदूत आरू महावाणिज्य दूत भी शामिल छै । एहि मे स 47टा विदेश सेवा स बाहर क अधिकारी क कब्जा मे अछि। एहि मे सिविल प्रशासन सेवा स सात संयुक्त सचिव, सात सैन्य अटैच, एकटा पुलिस परामर्शदाता, एकटा खुफिया परामर्शदाता, नौ प्रशासनिक उपसचिव, दूटा राजस्व उपसचिव, एकटा कानूनी उपसचिव, एकटा खाता उपसचिव, नौटा प्रशासनिक अनुभाग अधिकारी, तीनटा खाता अधिकारी, एकटा राजस्व अनुभाग अधिकारी आ पांचटा प्रशासनिक/खाता सहायक शामिल छथि।

मंत्रालय द्वारा भेजल गेल विदेश सेवा के कर्मी के अलावा मिशन स्थानीय कर्मचारी के सेहो नियुक्ति करैत अछि. एहि मे कार्यालय सचिव, कानूनी सलाहकार, दूत, अनुवादक, माली, सुरक्षा गार्ड आ कार्यालय सहायक आदि शामिल छथि ।

स्थानीय कर्मचारी क लेल 374 पद स्वीकृत अछि। विदेशी रोजगार बोर्ड कतार, सऊदी अरब, यूएई आ मलेशिया सहित पैघ संख्या मे नेपाली प्रवासी मजदूर वाला देश मे मिशन मे स्थानीय कर्मचारी कए आर्थिक सहयोग दैत आबि रहल छल। बोर्ड विभिन्न दूतावास मे 19 स्थानीय कर्मचारी कए फंडिंग करबा लेल सालाना 25.7 मिलियन टका खर्च करैत आबि रहल छल। लेकिन महालेखा परीक्षक केरऽ कार्यालय न॑ ई व्यवस्था क॑ नियम के विपरीत मानला के बाद बोर्ड द्वारा वित्त पोषित कर्मचारी के संख्या म॑ पिछला साल स॑ कटौती करलऽ गेलै, जेकरा स॑ सीमित कूटनीतिक कर्मचारी प॑ काम के बोझ आरू बढ़ी गेलै ।

सरकार सब 17 मंत्रालय क लेल नव संगठनात्मक आ प्रबंधन (ओ एंड एम) सर्वेक्षण केलक अछि। चूँकि एहि सर्वेक्षण क मकसद सार्वजनिक खर्च मे कटौती कैल गेल छल, एहि लेल विदेश मंत्रालय बेसी कर्मचारी क आग्रह क बावजूद पद नहि जोड़ि सकल अछि।

मंत्रालय न॑ बंद करै लेली प्रस्तावित छह मिशनऽ स॑ विदेश सेवा कर्मचारी क॑ दूतावासऽ म॑ स्थानांतरित करै के कोशिश करलकै, जहां अतिरिक्त कर्मी के जरूरत छै । मुदा ओ एंड एम पुनर्गठन के एखन धरि प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय सं प्रमाणित नहिं भेला के कारण मंत्रालय के योजना एखन धरि साकार नहिं भेल अछि. विदेश मंत्रालय क प्रवक्ता क्षेत्री कहला जे मंत्रालय बंद करबाक लेल प्रस्तावित मिशन स कर्मचारी कए जरूरतमंद लोक तक स्थानांतरित करि राज्य पर अतिरिक्त आर्थिक बोझ नहि लगेने चाहैत अछि।

एहि प्रस्ताव क तहत मंत्रालय मिशन पर प्रशासन, राजस्व आ लेखा समूह मे पद मे सेहो कटौती करत आ ओकर जगह पर विदेश सेवा क कर्मी सेहो राखत। नई दिल्ली आ बीजिंग मे नेपाली दूतावास मे दूटा मंत्री (आर्थिक) पद, हांगकांग, ल्हासा, कोलकाता, चेंगदू आ ग्वांगझौ मे पांचटा महावाणिज्य दूतावास, आ प्रशासनिक सेवा स सातटा संयुक्त सचिव स्तरीय पद खत्म करबाक प्रस्ताव रखने अछि।

एकरा म॑ सियोल, कुआलालंपुर, रियाद, दोहा आरू अबू धाबी म॑ सामान्य प्रशासन समूह म॑ श्रम परामर्शदाता के पदऽ के साथ-साथ नई दिल्ली म॑ सांस्कृतिक परामर्शदाता, विशाखापत्तनम म॑ आर्थिक परामर्शदाता, आरू वाशिंगटन, डीसी, आरू कोलकाता म॑ राजस्व समूह केरऽ नौ प्रशासनिक उपसचिव पदऽ प॑ कटौती करै के प्रस्ताव भी देलऽ गेलऽ छै । एहि प्रस्ताव मे विभिन्न मिशन मे दसटा प्रशासनिक अनुभाग अधिकारी पद मे कटौती करबाक सेहो कहल गेल अछि।

प्रशासनिक सेवा क अधिकारी प्रस्तावित कटौती क विरोध केलथि अछि। प्रशासनिक सेवा केरऽ दबाव के मतलब ई भी होय गेलऽ छै कि मुख्य सचिव गोविंदा बहादुर कार्की न॑ अभी तलक विदेश मंत्रालय केरऽ ओ एंड एम प्रस्ताव क॑ प्रमाणित नै करी सकलऽ छै ।

full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug 20: Minister for Information and Communications, Dr Bikram Timilsina, has said the public service broadcasting (PSB) entities- Nepal Television and Radio Nepal- must be professional, competitive, effective and accountable to the people. Minister Dr Timilsina stressed that all public institutions which are slow off the mark need improving for efficient services.

The Minister said it while garnering information about the budget and programmes set by the PSB entities for the current fiscal year. He said PSB entities should focus on their major objectives. "Media is currently expanding rapidly on digital platforms and social media, so Nepal Television and Radio Nepal can also augment quality of their contents with vibrant digital presence.

Minister Dr Timilsina directed the concerned officials to achieve best results with utmost use of available means and resources. Integration of administration and accounting departments of Nepal Television and Radio Nepal could be an option for transformation, he suggested. He urged the officials to keep in centre the institutional interests.

"Once the institution is strengthened, it ensures benefit to everyone. So, only pouring money by State into the institution cannot be a sustainable measure to achieve its objectives," the Minister reminded.

He further expected impartial, factual and objective news stories from PSB. The materials under political influence or biasness should not be broadcast, he said, directing the PSB officials to produce news and programmes that keep in centre the citizens. Investigative and public interest materials deserve equal priority, Dr Timilsina added.

The Minister also made aware the PSB entities to play role in curbing the misleading information that is spread specially through social media. Dissemination of early warning, information on relief and rescue on disasters are other priorities.

He pledged government support in developing PSB as a capable organization.

Joint secretary at the Ministry and member of the PSB, Ravi Lal Sharma, also spoke on need for new thoughts and programmes. The annual audit of the organization should be accomplished on time, he added.

Acting Chairperson of PSB, Urbashi Bashnyat, shared that she was making utmost effort to bolster image of PSB entities. (RSS)

काठमांडू, २० गते, सूचना तथा संचारमन्त्री डा. बिक्रम तिमिल्सिना जनसेवा प्रसारण संस्था- नेपाल टेलिभिजन आ रेडियो नेपाल- व्यावसायिक, प्रतिस्पर्धी, प्रभावी आ जनताके प्रति जवाबदेह होबाक चाही बतौलनि अछि । मंत्री डॉ. तिमिलसिना एहि बात पर जोर देलनि जे, जे सब सार्वजनिक संस्थान निशान स धीमा अछि, ओकरा कुशल सेवा लेल सुधार करबाक जरूरत अछि।

मंत्री जी ई बात पीएसबी संस्था द्वारा चालू वित्तीय वर्ष के लेल निर्धारित बजट आ कार्यक्रम के बारे मे जानकारी जुटाबैत कहलनि। ओ कहला जे पीएसबी क संस्था कए अपन प्रमुख उद्देश्य पर ध्यान देबाक चाही। "मीडिया एखन डिजिटल प्लेटफॉर्म आ सोशल मीडिया पर तेजी स विस्तार क रहल अछि, ताहि लेल नेपाल टेलीविजन आ रेडियो नेपाल सेहो जीवंत डिजिटल उपस्थिति स अपन सामग्री क गुणवत्ता कए बढ़ा सकैत अछि।"

मंत्री डॉ. तिमिल्सिना संबंधित अधिकारी कए उपलब्ध साधन आ संसाधन क बेसी स बेसी उपयोग क बेहतरीन परिणाम हासिल करबाक निर्देश देलथि। नेपाल टेलिभिजन आ रेडियो नेपालके प्रशासन आ लेखा विभागके एकीकरण परिवर्तनके विकल्प भऽ सकैत अछि ओ सुझाव देलनि । ओ अधिकारी स संस्थागत हित कए केंद्र मे रखबाक आग्रह केलथि।

"एक बेर संस्था मजबूत भ गेलाक बाद सबके लाभ सुनिश्चित करैत अछि।" अतः, केवल राज्य द्वारा संस्था में पैसा डालना ही ओकरऽ उद्देश्य प्राप्त करै के टिकाऊ उपाय नै होय सकै छै ।'

आगू हुनका पीएसबी स निष्पक्ष, तथ्यात्मक आ वस्तुनिष्ठ समाचार क उम्मीद छल। राजनीतिक प्रभाव या पूर्वाग्रह के तहत सामग्री के प्रसारण नै होबाक चाही, ओ पीएसबी के अधिकारी के निर्देश देलखिन जे नागरिक के केंद्र में राखय वाला खबर आ कार्यक्रम तैयार करथि। डॉ. तिमिल्सिना आगू कहलनि जे, जांच आ जनहित सामग्री समान प्राथमिकता के हकदार अछि।

मंत्री जी पीएसबी के संस्था सब के सेहो जागरूक केलनि जे सोशल मीडिया के माध्यम सं विशेष रूप सं फैलल भ्रामक जानकारी पर लगाम लगेबा मे भूमिका निभाबय. शीघ्र चेतावनी कें प्रसार, आपदाक पर राहत आ बचाव कें जानकारी अन्य प्राथमिकता छै.

ओ पीएसबी कए एकटा सक्षम संगठन क रूप मे विकसित करबा मे सरकारी सहयोग क वचन देलथि।

मंत्रालय के संयुक्त सचिव आ पीएसबी के सदस्य रवि लाल शर्मा सेहो नव विचार आ कार्यक्रम के जरूरत पर अपन बात रखलखिन्ह. ओ इहो कहलनि जे, संस्थाक वार्षिक लेखा परीक्षा समय पर पूरा हेबाक चाही।

पीएसबी केरऽ कार्यवाहक अध्यक्ष उर्बाशी बश्न्यात न॑ साझा करलकै कि हुनी पीएसबी केरऽ इकाइयऽ के छवि क॑ मजबूत करै के पूरा प्रयास करी रहलऽ छै । (आर एस एस) २.

title: Nepal Investment Mega Bank CEO Jyotiprakash Pandey Released on Bail - Ratopati
description: Nepal Investment Mega Bank CEO Jyotiprakash Pandey Released on Bail  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal Investment Mega Bank Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Jyotiprakash Pandey has been released on bail. A bench of Kathmandu District Court Judge Kamal Kant Joshi had demanded a bail of 80 lakh rupees from Pandey on Thursday. Pandey, who was arrested on charges of irregularities in the auction process of Smart Cell, has been ordered by the Kathmandu District Court to be released on a bail of 80 lakh rupees.

Pandey has been released after submitting a bank guarantee equal to the amount demanded by the court. He will now undergo trial outside of detention.

What is the case?

Smart Telecom Pvt. Ltd., which obtained an basic telephone service license from the Nepal Telecommunications Authority on April 2, 2070 BS, had its license automatically canceled from May 17, 2080 BS, as it did not renew the license as per regulations. After the cancellation of the license, as per the regulations, all the company's assets, infrastructure, and telecommunication network were taken under the control of the authority.

Pandey, who is also the chairman of the Loan Recovery Committee (LRC) formed to recover the loan given by Nepal Investment Mega Bank to Smart Telecom, was accused of irregularities in the auction process. The police had investigated him on the grounds that the auction process was carried out with the intention of fraudulently terminating the rights over the property that had come under the ownership of the Government of Nepal.

During the police investigation, it was found that the auction notice published by the bank on October 20, 2082 BS included approximately 40 crore rupees that Smart Cell owed to the landlords for house rent and electricity bills in the bid amount. The police claimed that although the bank recovered the amount, it has not yet paid the concerned landlords and attempted to cause damage to government property.

Earlier, in the same case, the police had arrested Pandey and submitted the investigation report to the government attorney's office. Hearing the same case, the court decided to release him on bail.

काठमांडू। नेपाल इन्वेस्टमेंट मेगा बैंक के मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी (सीईओ) ज्योतिप्रकाश पाण्डेय जमानत पर रिहा भेल अछि । काठमांडू जिल्ला न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश कमल कांत जोशी के पीठ गुरुवार के पाण्डेय स 80 लाख रुपया के जमानत के मांग केने छल। स्मार्ट सेल के नीलामी प्रक्रिया मे अनियमितता के आरोप मे गिरफ्तार पाण्डेय के काठमांडू जिल्ला न्यायालय 80 लाख रुपैया के जमानत पर रिहा करबाक आदेश देलक अछि।

पाण्डेय के कोर्ट के मांग के बराबर बैंक गारंटी जमा करला के बाद रिहा क देल गेल अछि. आब हुनका पर नजरबंदी स बाहर मुकदमा होएत।

की हाल अछि ?

स्मार्ट दूरसंचार प्रा. लिमिटेड, जे नेपाल दूरसंचार प्राधिकरण स 2 अप्रैल, 2070 बीएस कए बेसिक टेलीफोन सेवा लाइसेंस प्राप्त केने छल, ओकर लाइसेंस 17 मई, 2080 बीएस स स्वतः रद्द भ गेल छल, किया कि ओ नियम क अनुसार लाइसेंस क नवीकरण नहि केलक। लाइसेंस रद्द करला के बाद नियम के अनुसार कंपनी के सब संपत्ति, बुनियादी ढांचा, आ दूरसंचार नेटवर्क के प्राधिकरण के नियंत्रण में राखल गेल.

नेपाल इन्वेस्टमेंट मेगा बैंक द्वारा स्मार्ट टेलीकॉम के देल गेल ऋण वसूली के लेल गठित ऋण वसूली समिति (एलआरसी) के अध्यक्ष सेहो रहल पाण्डेय पर नीलामी प्रक्रिया मे गड़बड़ी के आरोप लागल छल। नेपाल सरकारक स्वामित्वमे आयल सम्पत्तिक अधिकारकेँ धोखाधड़ीसँ समाप्त करबाक उद्देश्यसँ नीलामी प्रक्रिया कएल गेल एहि आधारमे प्रहरी हुनकर जाँच केने छल ।

पुलिस जांच के दौरान पता चलल जे बैंक द्वारा 20 अक्टूबर, 2082 बीएस कए प्रकाशित नीलामी नोटिस मे लगभग 40 करोड़ रुपया शामिल अछि जे स्मार्ट सेल कए मकान मालिक कए बोली राशि मे मकान किराया आ बिजली बिल क बकाया छल। पुलिस के दावा अछि जे बैंक भले राशि बरामद केलक मुदा एखन धरि संबंधित मकान मालिक के भुगतान नहि केलक अछि आ सरकारी संपत्ति के नुकसान पहुंचेबाक प्रयास केलक अछि।

एहि सं पहिने ओही मामला मे पुलिस पांडेय के गिरफ्तार क जांच रिपोर्ट सरकारी वकील के कार्यालय मे जमा केने छल. ओही मामला के सुनवाई करैत कोर्ट हुनका जमानत पर रिहा करबाक फैसला केलक।

title: Bangladeshi scientist receives UK exploration award for Nepal Indigenous knowledge project - The Daily Star
description: Bangladeshi scientist receives UK exploration award for Nepal Indigenous knowledge project  The Daily Star
publisher.title: The Daily Star
full_article:
Abdullah Rubaet Chowdhury, a Bangladeshi social scientist and anthropologist, has received the SES Elodie Sandford Award from the UK-based Scientific Exploration Society (SES) for a planned research expedition documenting Indigenous ecological knowledge in Nepal’s Himalayan Mustang region.

The award will support a year-long expedition focused on Nepal's Bönpo community, which is home to one of the world’s oldest continuous knowledge traditions dating back 18,000 years, and its approaches to the natural environment.

Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source

Rubaet Chowdhury said the research would examine how Bönpo practitioners respond to environmental and climatic changes through knowledge rooted in their relationship with nature.

“Our expedition is particularly interested in learning how Bönpo practitioners, placed at the forefront of the climate crisis, have maintained a strong kinship with nature and natural entities driven by their ‘living knowledge’ to face these challenges,” he said.

The expedition is expected to take place in the Mustang region around the Kali Gandaki Gorge, an environmentally and culturally distinctive area of the trans-Himalayan landscape.

According to the expedition team, the project will use a collaborative research model intended to avoid treating Indigenous knowledge simply as information to be extracted by outside researchers.

Rubaet Chowdhury and his team plan to work with Bön spiritual leaders and young people using an ethnophotography-based approach. The researchers say they will jointly develop biodiversity conservation indicators, participatory maps and a community-owned field film.

The project aims to connect local environmental practices with contemporary biodiversity policy while allowing the community to retain ownership of the knowledge and materials produced during the research.

Findings from the expedition are expected to be shared with bodies involved in implementing the UN Global Biodiversity Framework, including the secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity, as well as Nepal’s Ministry of Forests and Environment, according to the press release.

The team also plans exhibitions and academic presentations, including at Heidelberg University’s ethnographic museum and institutions in Nepal.

The Scientific Exploration Society is a UK organisation that supports expeditions combining scientific research, exploration and conservation.

बांग्लादेशी सामाजिक वैज्ञानिक आरू मानवशास्त्री अब्दुल्ला रुबेत चौधरी क॑ नेपाल केरऽ हिमालयन मस्टैंग क्षेत्र म॑ स्वदेशी पारिस्थितिकी ज्ञान के दस्तावेजीकरण करै वाला योजनाबद्ध शोध अभियान लेली यूके स्थित वैज्ञानिक अन्वेषण सोसाइटी (एसईएस) स॑ एसईएस एलोडी सैंडफोर्ड पुरस्कार मिललऽ छै ।

ई पुरस्कार नेपाल केरऽ बोनपो समुदाय, जे १८,००० साल पुरानऽ दुनिया केरऽ सबसें पुरानऽ निरंतर ज्ञान परंपरा म॑ स॑ एक के घर छै, आरू प्राकृतिक पर्यावरण के प्रति एकरऽ दृष्टिकोण प॑ केंद्रित साल भर के अभियान क॑ समर्थन देतै ।

द डेली स्टार के विश्वसनीय स्रोत के रूप में जोड़य लेल एतय टैप करू

रुबाएत चौधरी नँ कहलकै कि ई शोध मँ ई जांच करलौ जैतै कि बोनपो के व्यवसायी प्रकृति के साथ अपनौ संबंध मँ जड़ जमाय वाला ज्ञान के माध्यम स॑ पर्यावरण आरू जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रति कोन तरह के प्रतिक्रिया दै छै ।

हुनी कहलकै, “हमरऽ अभियान ई जानय मँ विशेष रूप स॑ दिलचस्पी रखै छै कि जलवायु संकट म॑ सबसें आगू रखलऽ गेलऽ बोनपो केरऽ व्यवसायी न॑ ई चुनौती के सामना करै लेली अपनऽ ‘जीवित ज्ञान’ स॑ संचालित प्रकृति आरू प्राकृतिक इकाइयऽ के साथ मजबूत रिश्तेदारी क॑ कोना कायम रखन॑ छै ।

ई अभियान हिमालय पार केरऽ परिदृश्य केरऽ पर्यावरण आरू सांस्कृतिक रूप स॑ विशिष्ट क्षेत्र काली गंडकी गॉर्ज के आसपास के मस्टैंग क्षेत्र म॑ होय के उम्मीद छै ।

अभियान टीम के अनुसार ई परियोजना म॑ सहयोगात्मक शोध मॉडल के उपयोग करलऽ जैतै जेकरऽ उद्देश्य स्वदेशी ज्ञान क॑ खाली बाहरी शोधकर्ता सिनी द्वारा निकालै वाला जानकारी के रूप म॑ नै मानलऽ जाय ।

रुबेत चौधरी आरू हुनकऽ टीम न॑ नृवंशविज्ञान आधारित दृष्टिकोण के उपयोग करी क॑ बोन आध्यात्मिक नेता आरू युवा सिनी के साथ काम करै के योजना बना रहलऽ छै । शोधकर्ता सब के कहना छै कि हुनी संयुक्त रूप स॑ जैव विविधता संरक्षण सूचक, भागीदारी वाला नक्शा आरू समुदाय के स्वामित्व वाला फील्ड फिल्म तैयार करतै ।

परियोजना कें उद्देश्य स्थानीय पर्यावरण प्रथाक कें समकालीन जैव विविधता नीति सं जोड़नाय छै आ संगहि समुदाय कें शोध कें दौरान उत्पादित ज्ञान आ सामग्री कें स्वामित्व बरकरार रखनाय छै.

प्रेस विज्ञप्ति मे कहल गेल अछि जे एहि अभियान सँ प्राप्त निष्कर्ष संयुक्त राष्ट्र वैश्विक जैव विविधता ढाँचा लागू करबा मे लागल निकाय मे साझा करबाक उम्मीद अछि, जाहि मे जैविक विविधता महासन्धिक सचिवालयक संग-संग नेपालक वन आ पर्यावरण मंत्रालय सेहो शामिल अछि ।

टीम न॑ प्रदर्शनी आरू शैक्षणिक प्रस्तुति के योजना भी बनाबै छै, जेकरा म॑ हाइडलबर्ग विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ नृवंशविज्ञान संग्रहालय आरू नेपाल केरऽ संस्थानऽ म॑ भी शामिल छै ।

वैज्ञानिक अन्वेषण सोसाइटी यूके केरऽ एगो संगठन छेकै जे वैज्ञानिक अनुसंधान, अन्वेषण आरू संरक्षण के संयोजन वाला अभियानऽ के समर्थन करै छै ।

title: DICL to extract 96 million tonnes iron ore - The Rising Nepal
description: DICL to extract 96 million tonnes iron ore  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug 20: Dhaubadi Iron Company Limited has prepared a plan for mining iron ore at its mining site located in Hupsekot Rural Municipality-5, Dhaubadi, Nawalparasi.

The company has submitted a report to the Department of Mines and Geology with a plan to extract 96 million tonnes of iron ore from the mine spread over about 41 square kilometers.

The mining area has been divided into two parts: the Dhaubadi Pokhari block and the Durlung block. The Dhaubadi Pokhari block covers 25 square kilometers, while the Durlung block spans 16 square kilometers. After this plan is approved, the company has said it will carry out further exploration and mining operations related to the iron deposits.

Dhaubadi Iron Company Limited was established in 2076BS with the aim of commercially producing iron. It is an undertaking of the Government of Nepal. The company's director, Shailesh Kumar Thapa, informed that drilling work of 1,500 meters was completed at 12 different locations to test underground iron ore samples.

The company has stated that the environmental impact assessment work is currently underway and the work to prepare the Detailed Project Report (DPR) will also be started soon.

Director Thapa said that once the mine is operational, the iron products produced are expected to replace about 25 percent of the country's overall import demand.

He believes that mining operations will create a large number of jobs and contribute to the national economy. The company has stated that the necessary infrastructure and road upgrades to reach the mine are underway. (RSS)

title: Nepal’s journalism classrooms are emptying out - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepal’s journalism classrooms are emptying out  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
In the academic year 2020-21, journalism and mass communication were taught at 74 campuses affiliated with Tribhuvan University across the country. The number fell to 61 in 2023-24 and declined further to just 57 by 2024-25.

Purbanchal University has seen a similar trend. Its journalism and mass communication enrolment fell from 122 students in 2021-22 to 74 in 2025-26.

At St Xavier’s College in Maitighar, journalism department head Chun Bahadur Gurung has seen the change in his own classroom. “We have taught as many as 34 students in a batch, but now the average is around 14 or 15,” he said.

Teachers and college administrators point to several reasons: shrinking number of media outlets, low salaries, delayed payments, insecure jobs, the growing preference for overseas education, and stronger demand for subjects perceived to offer clearer career paths.

“Most students who come to us for counselling ask which subject would be best if they want to go abroad,” said Acharya. “Out of 1,000 students, perhaps only one shows interest in journalism.”

For many students, the attraction of foreign education is reinforced by the perception that journalism offers few secure career opportunities at home. The wider media industry has struggled to create stable jobs and decent working conditions.

“Journalism itself is in a problematic state,” said Rishikesh Dahal, an associate professor at TU’s Department of Journalism and Mass Communication. “Many media outlets have disappeared and there is no longer the competition we saw before. It is natural for students to turn away from such an uncertain profession.”

According to Dahal, the media sector is struggling not only with a shrinking business model, but also with a severe erosion of public trust. "The 2015 earthquake served as an early warning for the media industry, but we failed to prepare, and the Covid pandemic subsequently hit us hard," he said.

The economic difficulties have also changed how journalists work and how audiences consume news. Social media has made publishing and distributing information easier than ever, while weakening the traditional boundaries between journalism, commentary, entertainment and influence.

Nepal’s media sector came under severe pressure during the Covid pandemic, while the September 2025 Gen Z protests brought further destruction. Journalists were injured and several newsrooms were attacked or burned during the unrest.

Dipesh Acharya, proprietor of the College of Journalism and Mass Communication (CJMC), however, argues that this should strengthen rather than weaken the case for professional journalism.

“Access to information has expanded greatly, but misleading information and clickbait content have also increased,” he said. “In such a situation, the role of professional journalism is even more important. But we need to create an environment in which the new generation entering the field can stay.”

The challenge, educators say, is that journalism education has not kept pace with changes in the industry.

Manju Mishra, founding principal of CJMC, said social media and new technology had transformed the way information was produced and distributed, but universities and journalism programmes had not adapted at the same speed.

“There is a wide gap between what is taught in classrooms and what happens in real newsrooms,” said Mishra. “Without regular internships, newsroom-based practice and access to modern communication tools, it is difficult to make journalism education relevant and market-oriented.”

Gurung agrees that the curriculum needs a major overhaul. “We need to ask what kind of curriculum we are teaching,” he said. “Is the course suited to the times, or are we still following an old syllabus? A market-oriented and contemporary curriculum is essential.”

In his experience, students are increasingly more interested in content creation than traditional journalism. That shift, he said, should not simply be treated as a threat. Journalism education could use it to teach students how to report, verify and distribute credible information across multiple platforms.

“Journalism is not just an academic subject,” said Gurung. “It produces skilled people who protect citizens’ right to information, uphold accountability and keep public debate alive.”

The history of journalism education in Nepal is much older than today’s digital media landscape. The institutional development of Nepali journalism is generally traced to the publication of Sudha Sagar in 1898 and Gorkhapatra in 1901. Formal academic journalism education began later at Ratna Rajya Laxmi Campus, where journalism was introduced at certificate level in 1976. Bachelor’s-level study followed in 1981 and master’s-level study in 2001.

Prateek Pradhan, editor-in-chief of news website Baahrakhari, said the weakness of media institutions themselves was partly responsible for the declining appeal of journalism as a career. “Media organisations have not been able to properly operate financially, so they could not pay salaries on time,” said Pradhan. “As a result, the idea has grown that perhaps one should not study journalism.”

He also warned that the public image of journalism suffers when people without a clear understanding of professional ethics become prominent through social media.

“If people can do whatever they want without understanding journalism’s principles and values, and those people gain prominence, it discourages students from studying journalism,” he said. “There has been little effort to say that journalism is worth studying or that journalism must be kept alive.”

On paper, Nepal is doing better than most of its neighbours. In practice, the space for journalism is tightening.

As the world marked World Press Freedom Day on May 3, Nepal’s position in the latest World Press Freedom Index 2026 offered a measure of reassurance. Published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), the index places Nepal 87th out of 180 countries, the highest in South Asia.

“Journalism must not die, especially at a time when democracy is under pressure globally,” said Gurung. “It is not dead. I would rather say it is changing. We need a multidisciplinary approach that matches the times and responds to what the market needs.”

शैक्षणिक वर्ष 2020-21 मे देश भरिक त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय सँ जुड़ल 74 परिसर मे पत्रकारिता आ जनसंचारक पढ़ाई भेल। 2023-24 मे इ संख्या 61 भ गेल आ 2024-25 तक इ संख्या आओर घटि कए महज 57 भ गेल।

पूर्वांचल विश्वविद्यालय मे सेहो एहने रुझान देखल गेल अछि। एकर पत्रकारिता आ जनसंचार नामांकन 2021-22 मे 122 छात्र स घटि कए 2025-26 मे 74 भ गेल।

मैतीघर के सेंट जेवियर कॉलेज मे पत्रकारिता विभाग के प्रमुख चुन बहादुर गुरुंग अपनहि कक्षा मे बदलाव देखलखिन्ह. ओ कहला जे हम एक बैच मे 34टा छात्र कए पढ़ा चुकल छी, मुदा आब औसत 14 या 15 क आसपास अछि।

शिक्षक आरू कॉलेज प्रशासक कई कारणऽ के तरफ इशारा करै छै: मीडिया केरऽ संख्या म॑ कमी, कम वेतन, भुगतान म॑ देरी, असुरक्षित नौकरी, विदेशी शिक्षा केरऽ बढ़तऽ पसंद, आरू ऐन्हऽ विषयऽ के मजबूत मांग जेकरा स॑ स्पष्ट कैरियर केरऽ रास्ता मिलै वाला मानलऽ जाय छै ।

आचार्य कहलनि जे, हमरा सब लग काउंसलिंग लेल आबय वाला अधिकांश छात्र पूछैत छथि जे अगर ओ विदेश जेबाक इच्छा रखैत छथि त कोन विषय बेसी नीक रहत। “1000 छात्र मे स शायद एकटा छात्र पत्रकारिता मे रुचि देखाबैत अछि।”

बहुत सारा छात्रऽ लेली विदेशी शिक्षा के आकर्षण क॑ ई धारणा स॑ मजबूत करलऽ जाय छै कि पत्रकारिता घरऽ म॑ ही कैरियर केरऽ सुरक्षित अवसर कम दै छै । व्यापक मीडिया उद्योग स्थिर रोजगार आ सभ्य काजक स्थिति पैदा करबा मे संघर्ष केलक अछि।

टीयू केरऽ पत्रकारिता आरू जनसंचार विभाग केरऽ एसोसिएट प्रोफेसर ऋषिकेश दाहाल न॑ कहलकै कि पत्रकारिता ही समस्याग्रस्त स्थिति म॑ छै । ओ कहलनि जे, बहुत रास मीडिया गायब भ गेल अछि आ आब ओ प्रतिस्पर्धा नहि अछि जे हम सब पहिने देखलहुं, एहन अनिश्चित पेशे स छात्र क मुँह मोड़ब स्वाभाविक अछि।”

दाहाल के अनुसार मीडिया क्षेत्र न सिर्फ सिकुड़ैत बिजनेस मॉडल स जूझि रहल अछि, बल्कि जन विश्वास के गंभीर क्षरण स सेहो जूझि रहल अछि। ओ कहलनि जे, 2015 के भूकंप मीडिया उद्योग के लेल एकटा शुरुआती चेतावनी के काज केलक, मुदा हम सब तैयारी में असफल रहलहुं, आ एकर बाद कोविड महामारी हमरा सब पर बहुत मारलक।

आर्थिक कठिनाई के कारण पत्रकार के काज करय के तरीका आओर दर्शक खबर के कोना उपभोग करय छथिन्ह ओहि मे सेहो बदलाव आयल अछि. सोशल मीडिया सूचना प्रकाशन आ वितरण के काज पहिने स बेसी आसान बना देलक अछि, संगहि पत्रकारिता, टिप्पणी, मनोरंजन आ प्रभाव के बीच पारंपरिक सीमा के कमजोर क देलक अछि।

कोविड महामारी के समय नेपाल के मीडिया क्षेत्र पर घोर दबाव आयल छल, जखन कि सितम्बर 2025 के जेन जेड विरोध प्रदर्शन आओर तबाही केने छल. अशांति के दौरान पत्रकार घायल भ गेल आओर कईटा न्यूजरूम पर हमला या जरा देल गेल.

कॉलेज ऑफ जर्नलिज्म एंड मास कम्युनिकेशन (सीजेएमसी) के मालिक दिपेश आचार्य के तर्क छै कि हालांकि ई पेशेवर पत्रकारिता के मामला क॑ कमजोर नै करी क॑ मजबूत होना चाहियऽ ।

ओ कहला जे सूचना तक पहुंच मे काफी विस्तार भेल अछि, मुदा भ्रामक जानकारी आ क्लिकबेट क सामग्री मे सेहो बढ़ोतरी भेल अछि। ओ कहला जे एहन स्थिति मे पेशेवर पत्रकारिता क भूमिका आओर बेसी जरूरी अछि।मुदा हमरा सब कए एहन माहौल बनेबाक जरूरत अछि जाहि मे एहि क्षेत्र मे प्रवेश करय वाला नव पीढ़ी रहि सकए।”

शिक्षाविद के कहनाय छनि जे चुनौती ई अछि जे पत्रकारिता के शिक्षा एहि उद्योग मे बदलाव के संग तालमेल नहि बना सकल अछि.

सीजेएमसी के संस्थापक प्रधानाध्यापक मंजू मिश्रा कहलनि जे सोशल मीडिया आ नव तकनीक सं सूचना के उत्पादन आ वितरण के तरीका मे बदलाव आयल अछि, मुदा विश्वविद्यालय आ पत्रकारिता के कार्यक्रम ओहि गति सं अनुकूल नहि भेल अछि.

मिश्र कहलनि जे, कक्षा मे जे किछु पढ़ाओल जाइत अछि आ असली न्यूजरूम मे जे किछु होइत अछि ताहि मे बहुत अंतर अछि। “नियमित इंटर्नशिप, न्यूजरूम आधारित अभ्यास आरू आधुनिक संचार उपकरण तक पहुँच के बिना पत्रकारिता शिक्षा क॑ प्रासंगिक आरू बाजार-उन्मुख बनाना मुश्किल छै।”

गुरुंग एहि बात स सहमत छथि जे पाठ्यक्रम मे पैघ ओवरहाल क जरूरत अछि। ओ कहला जे हमरा सब कए इ पूछबाक जरूरत अछि जे हम सब कोन तरहक पाठ्यक्रम पढ़ा रहल छी। “की कोर्स समय के अनुकूल अछि, या हम सब एखनो पुरान सिलेबस के पालन क रहल छी? बाजार उन्मुख आ समकालीन पाठ्यक्रम अनिवार्य अछि।”

हुनकऽ अनुभव म॑ पारंपरिक पत्रकारिता स॑ अधिक सामग्री निर्माण म॑ छात्रऽ के रुचि तेजी स॑ बढ़ी रहलऽ छै । ओ कहला जे ओहि बदलाव कए खाली खतरा नहि मानल जेबाक चाही। पत्रकारिता शिक्षा एकरऽ उपयोग छात्रऽ क॑ सिखाबै लेली करी सकै छै कि कईएक प्लेटफॉर्म प॑ विश्वसनीय जानकारी के रिपोर्टिंग, सत्यापन आरू वितरित करलऽ जाय ।

गुरुंग कहलनि जे, पत्रकारिता सिर्फ शैक्षणिक विषय नहि अछि। “ई कुशल लोग पैदा करै छै जे नागरिकऽ के सूचना के अधिकार के रक्षा करै छै, जवाबदेही के कायम रखै छै आरू सार्वजनिक बहस क॑ जिंदा रखै छै।”

नेपाल मे पत्रकारिता शिक्षाक इतिहास आजुक डिजिटल मीडिया परिदृश्य सँ बहुत पुरान अछि । नेपाली पत्रकारिता के संस्थागत विकास सामान्यतः १८९८ मे सुधा सागर आ १९०१ मे गोरखापत्रक प्रकाशन सँ भेटैत अछि ।बाद मे रत्न राज्य लक्ष्मी परिसर मे औपचारिक शैक्षणिक पत्रकारिता शिक्षा शुरू भेल, जतय सन् १९७६ मे प्रमाणपत्र स्तर पर पत्रकारिता शुरू भेल । एकर बाद 1981 मे स्नातक स्तर क अध्ययन आ 2001 मे स्नातकोत्तर स्तर क अध्ययन भेल ।

समाचार वेबसाइट बहराखरी के प्रधान संपादक प्रतीक प्रधान नँ कहलकै कि कैरियर के रूप मँ पत्रकारिता के आकर्षण घटै लेली खुद मीडिया संस्थान के कमजोरी कुछ हद तलक जिम्मेदार छै । प्रधान कहला जे मीडिया संगठन आर्थिक रूप स ठीक स काज नहि क सकल अछि, ताहि लेल ओ समय पर वेतन नहि द सकल। “फलस्वरूप ई विचार बढ़ि गेल अछि जे शायद पत्रकारिता के पढ़ाई नहि करबाक चाही।”

ओ इहो चेतावनी देलनि जे पत्रकारिता के सार्वजनिक छवि तखन नुकसान होइत अछि जखन पेशेवर नैतिकता के स्पष्ट समझ वाला लोक सोशल मीडिया के माध्यम सं प्रमुख भ जाइत छथिन्ह.

ओ कहलनि जे, जौं पत्रकारिता के सिद्धांत आ मूल्य के बिना बुझने लोक जे चाहय से क सकैत छथि, आ ओ लोक के प्रमुखता भेटैत छनि त ई छात्र के पत्रकारिता के पढ़ाई सं हतोत्साहित करैत अछि. “पत्रकारिता अध्ययन के लायक छै या पत्रकारिता के जिंदा रखना जरूरी छै, ई कहै के बहुत कम प्रयास करलऽ गेलऽ छै।”

कागज पर नेपाल अपन अधिकांश पड़ोसी देश स नीक काज क रहल अछि। व्यवहार मे पत्रकारिता के जगह कड़ा भ रहल अछि.

विश्व प्रेस स्वतन्त्रता दिवस ३ मई क॑ मनाबै के साथ ही नवीनतम विश्व प्रेस स्वतन्त्रता सूचकांक २०२६ म॑ नेपाल केरऽ स्थिति स॑ कुछ आश्वासन मिललै । रिपोर्टर्स विदाउट बॉर्डर्स (आरएसएफ) द्वारा प्रकाशित ई सूचकांक नेपाल क॑ १८० देशऽ म॑ स॑ ८७वां स्थान प॑ रखलकै, जे दक्षिण एशिया केरऽ सबस॑ अधिक छै ।

गुरुंग कहला जे पत्रकारिता कए नहि मरबाक चाही, खास कए एहन समय मे जखन लोकतंत्र पर वैश्विक स्तर पर दबाव अछि। "ई मरल नहि अछि। हम इ कहब जे इ बदलि रहल अछि। हमरा सब कए एकटा बहुविषयक दृष्टिकोण चाही जे समय क संग मेल खाए आ बाजार कए जे जरूरत अछि ओकर जवाब देए।"

title: Bangladesh envoy proposes cultural, creative exchange - The Rising Nepal
description: Bangladesh envoy proposes cultural, creative exchange  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Aug. 21: Ambassador of Bangladesh to Nepal Md. Shafiqur Rahman called for beginning an annual Bangladesh-Nepal Cultural and Creative Exchange Programme while addressing the inauguration of the “Beautiful Bangladesh” International Photo Exhibition 2026 on Wednesday at Kathmandu Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage site in Basantapur, Kathmandu.

The Beautiful Bangladesh International Photo Exhibition 2026 was jointly organised by the National Forum of Photo Journalists (NFPJ) Nepal and Bangladesh Photo Journalists Association (BPJA) as part of the Bangladesh-Nepal Photo Journalist Exchange Programme to strengthen friendship, professional collaboration, cultural understanding and tourism promotion between the two countries. The event also commemorated World Photography Day, according to a press statement from the Bangladesh Embassy in Kathmandu.

Acting Director General of the Nepal Tourism Board and Deputy Director of the Chinese Cultural Centre and dignitaries from Nepal and China also joined the event.

In his remarks as the Chief Guest, the Ambassador, highlighting the importance of photography as a powerful means of communication and expression, said the exhibition in a world heritage site on World Photography Day provides Nepali audiences with an opportunity to discover Bangladesh’s natural beauty, cultural heritage, historical landmarks and, most importantly, the everyday lives and aspirations of its people.

Recalling the deep cultural cooperation between Bangladesh and Nepal, he shed light on common values and cultural and linguistic affinities of the two countries. He lauded the increasing exchange of tourists, especially from Bangladesh to Nepal and added that people-to-people connectivity provides the major building block in the bilateral ties of the two neighbouring countries.

He made two specific proposals to further deepen cultural and people-to-people ties between the two countries. He proposed to consider establishing the Annual Cultural and Creative Exchange Programme to bring together photographers, filmmakers, musicians, artists, writers, and other cultural practitioners from Bangladesh and Nepal.

He suggested that the programme could include arranging joint exhibitions, cultural performances, film festivals, photography exchanges, and workshops, alternating between the two countries.

Congratulating NFPJ and BPJA for organising the exhibition on the occasion of World Photography Day, the Ambassador expressed hope that the exhibition would inspire greater interaction, two-way travel, professional cooperation and friendship between the peoples of Bangladesh and Nepal.

नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्ड के कार्यवाहक महानिदेशक आ चीनी सांस्कृतिक केन्द्र के उपनिदेशक आ नेपाल आ चीन के गणमान्य लोकनि सेहो एहि आयोजन मे शामिल भेलाह ।

मुख्य अतिथि के रूप मँ अपनौ टिप्पणी मँ राजदूत नँ संचार आरू अभिव्यक्ति के एगो सशक्त साधन के रूप मँ फोटोग्राफी के महत्व प प्रकाश डालतें हुअय कहलकै कि विश्व फोटोग्राफी दिवस प विश्व धरोहर स्थल मँ आयोजित प्रदर्शनी स॑ नेपाली दर्शक सिनी क॑ बांग्लादेश केरऽ प्राकृतिक सौंदर्य, सांस्कृतिक धरोहर, ऐतिहासिक स्थल आरू सबसें महत्वपूर्ण बात ई छै कि ओकरऽ लोगऽ के रोजमर्रा के जीवन आरू आकांक्षा के खोज करै के मौका मिलै छै ।

बांग्लादेश आ नेपालक बीच गहींर सांस्कृतिक सहयोगक स्मरण करैत ओ दुनू देशक साझा मूल्य आ सांस्कृतिक आ भाषाई आत्मीयता पर प्रकाश देलनि । हुनी खास करी क॑ बांग्लादेश स॑ नेपाल तलक पर्यटकऽ के बढ़तऽ आदान-प्रदान के प्रशंसा करतें हुअ॑ कहलकै कि लोगऽ स॑ लोगऽ के संपर्क दूनू पड़ोसी देशऽ के द्विपक्षीय संबंधऽ म॑ प्रमुख बिल्डिंग ब्लॉक प्रदान करै छै ।

दुनू देशक बीच सांस्कृतिक आ जन-जन संबंध केँ आओर गहींर करबाक लेल ओ दूटा विशिष्ट प्रस्ताव रखलनि । बांग्लादेश आरू नेपाल केरऽ फोटोग्राफर, फिल्म निर्माता, संगीतकार, कलाकार, लेखक, आरू अन्य सांस्कृतिक व्यवसायी सिनी क॑ एक साथ लानै लेली वार्षिक सांस्कृतिक आरू रचनात्मक आदान-प्रदान कार्यक्रम के स्थापना प॑ विचार करै के प्रस्ताव रखलकै ।

हुनकऽ सुझाव छेलै कि ई कार्यक्रम म॑ दूनू देशऽ के बीच बारी-बारी स॑ संयुक्त प्रदर्शनी, सांस्कृतिक प्रदर्शन, फिल्म महोत्सव, फोटोग्राफी आदान-प्रदान, आरू कार्यशाला के व्यवस्था करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै ।

विश्व फोटोग्राफी दिवस के अवसर पर एनएफपीजे आरू बीपीजेए क॑ ई प्रदर्शनी के आयोजन लेली बधाई दैत राजदूत न॑ आशा व्यक्त करलकै कि ई प्रदर्शनी स॑ बांग्लादेश आरू नेपाल के लोगऽ के बीच अधिक बातचीत, द्विपक्षीय यात्रा, पेशेवर सहयोग आरू दोस्ती के प्रेरणा मिलतै ।

title: Ronda Zelezny-Green on how Nepal’s teachers are using AI ‘almost blindly’ - The Kathmandu Post
description: Ronda Zelezny-Green on how Nepal’s teachers are using AI ‘almost blindly’  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Artificial intelligence is already finding its way into Nepal’s classrooms, even as the education system is still figuring out how to respond to it. Teachers and students are already using generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, according to Ronda Zelezny-Green, an international consultant specialising in AI in education and digital skills and the research lead for the British Council Nepal’s AI4ED project. The question, she says, is no longer whether AI should be used in education. It is how it can be used to improve learning without creating new problems. “The teachers are ready and open to using generative AI,” Zelezny-Green told The Post. “So now it’s about figuring out how to use it to advance education and learning.” The first phase of AI4ED involved a national mixed-methods study of 800 teachers. The research found that geography had less influence on AI use than expected. Teachers in urban and rural areas were using AI in broadly similar ways. Age, however, made a significant difference. Among teachers aged 30 or younger, 94 percent were described as fast AI adopters with experience using AI. Among those aged 50 or older, the figure fell to 54 percent. Perhaps more striking was what teachers themselves identified as the biggest obstacle. It was not infrastructure.



It was training. “They don’t know where to get training, and the government isn’t providing it,” Zelezny-Green said. “So they are using AI, but almost blindly.” The gap could become increasingly important as AI tools become more common in schools. Knowing how to operate an AI chatbot is not the same as knowing how to use it responsibly or effectively. Zelezny-Green, who has worked on digital skills and education technology across 80 countries, says teachers globally are struggling with the same problem, not just in Nepal. “There simply isn’t enough teacher training,” she said. For Nepal, that training needs to be designed around the country’s own education system rather than imported wholesale from technology companies. Teachers need to understand not only how to prompt an AI system, but also how to assess its answers, protect sensitive information, and recognise the ethical risks of using such tools. Data protection is one particular concern. Teachers may not realise that information entered into AI systems can be used for training or other purposes. Responsible AI adoption, therefore, cannot be limited to teachers. Schools, students, and parents all have a role to play. “It needs to be an ecosystem of responsibility shared among everyone who uses AI,” she said.

Zelezny-Green speaking at the ‘Teaching and Learning Futures Nepal: AI for Equitable Education’ conference in Kathmandu on August 18. Photo: Courtesy of The British Council Nepal

Nepal also faces another challenge—and an opportunity—in the language gap. Many of the most widely used AI systems perform far better in English than in Nepali and other local languages. Zelezny-Green says current tools can produce inaccurate translations and culturally unrealistic representations. But she sees that weakness as an opportunity for Nepal to develop its own solutions. Smaller language models can be cheaper to develop and maintain than the massive systems behind popular commercial chatbots. Nepal could potentially develop models designed specifically for Nepali and other local languages, using resources already available in the country. “You have Nepali books here. You have the resources, and the government could support this,” she said. The biggest challenge, she argues, would be access to the computing power needed to train such models—and the political will to make it happen. That leads to a broader question about who controls the technology, data and infrastructure on which AI depends. Zelezny-Green argues that Nepal should think seriously about “AI sovereignty”—the idea that countries should not become entirely dependent on foreign companies for AI technologies and infrastructure. “Wholesale reliance on foreign AI technologies, especially expensive American ones, will not be sustainable in the long run,” she said. But developing local technologies does not solve the question of how AI should be used in classrooms. One of the biggest changes may need to come from the way students are taught and assessed. For years, education systems have talked about the importance of creativity, collaboration and problem-solving. Generative AI makes those skills even more important because students can now outsource many conventional forms of homework to a chatbot. Instead of treating this only as a cheating problem, Zelezny-Green argues that schools need to rethink assessment itself. “If a teacher puts in little effort, why should a student work hard when they can simply ask ChatGPT or Claude to do their homework?” she said. She believes education needs “a new social contract” around AI. That does not mean abandoning foundational skills. In fact, she argues the opposite. Students first need strong foundations in reading and writing, critical thinking and critical media literacy. They need to be able to recognise misinformation, disinformation and AI-generated content before they can be expected to use AI responsibly. This is also why she rejects the idea of simply banning AI from schools. “One of my biggest pet peeves is the idea that we should simply ban AI,” she said. Even students who are not encouraged to use AI will encounter it outside school, she argues. They therefore need to understand what the technology is, what its risks are and how to use it responsibly.



For Nepal, that requires policy to catch up with practice.

Dipesh Darshandhari/TKP
